Identity.History: Blacksmithing was an important craft in ancient Athens, supporting agriculture, construction, warfare, and everyday life. Athenian smiths worked mainly with iron and bronze, producing tools, weapons, fittings, nails, and household goods in small workshops using charcoal-fired furnaces, anvils, hammers, and bellows. Metalworking was especially concentrated in busy craft districts such as the Kerameikos and around the Agora, where skilled artisans supplied both private customers and the needs of the state.
